text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1% today to $142.34, extending a two-week rally of nearly 14%. The driver is straightforward: oil prices surged on escalating geopolitical risk in the Middle East. Attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities have raised concerns about crude supply disruptions, pushing global oil prices to $125 per barrel—well above the U.S. benchmark of $96. As a major oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude prices climb.

The broader picture is a sustained supply squeeze. The International Energy Agency warned of market constraints, and analysts expect diesel shortages to persist into 2027 due to Iran-related disruption and falling inventories. In this environment, oil producers with the scale to capitalize on higher prices are seeing their valuations repriced upward.
